correctness.rationale: The proof identifies all Alexander-dual faces in dimensions <=4 and rules out higher ones. At girth five, stars and nonpentagon paths have private triangles; each pentagon creates a five-cycle of tetrahedra beneath one four-cell. It is removed by one free 4/3 collapse followed by four legal 3/2 collapses; forbidden short cycles exclude interference. The dual collapses integrally to a simply connected 2-complex with H2 free of Euler rank. Any six-set has a disconnected 4-set, giving the primal complete 2-skeleton. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality, Hurewicz and Whitehead prove the arbitrary-graph homotopy type. The clean standalone checker exhaustively reconstructs and verifies the collapse for 10 named and 300 deterministic additional examples, independently checks full mod-two dual homology for all named examples and primal homology for n<=10. Finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The newly proved universal claim is the integral sphere-wedge homotopy classification of ordinary four-cut complexes for all graphs of girth exactly five and order at least nine. Bayer et al. (2024) already obtained the pentagon-corrected face lattice and Euler characteristic; those alone do not exclude lower-dimensional homology or determine homotopy. The publicly available high-girth theorem applies to girth at least six and its single private-free-face argument does not apply to the pentagonal block. An earlier Petersen-specific four-cut calculation is a special case, not a separate new result. A different published-finding corpus four-cut study treats triangular graph girth three. Full scientific result texts and the 2024 pertinent primary PDF were compared. Unindexed equivalent or indirect stronger work remains a risk.

value.rationale: Sharp and mathematically motivated first boundary beyond the existing girth >=6 four-cut homotopy theorem. Pentagon overlaps prevent the old private-face argument; the new cyclic-block cancellation gives an all-graph integral sphere-wedge classification and rules out nontrivial lower homology, which the published five-cycle Euler correction does not decide. Includes structurally natural cubic girth-five graphs such as the dodecahedron, without presenting previously known Petersen values as new. The theorem need not establish shellability, module actions, or a larger cut-parameter classification to have value.
